style_when: the story is a single number, rule, gate or shift and restraint is the point — with no scene to photograph, the frame must still be a real assembly: a modular bay, an unlatched inspection gate, a rack of blades, an interlocking connector
prompt: Minimalist studio composition of a modular routing proxy bay on a weathered concrete plant floor, extreme asymmetry with the hero assembly off-centre. A brushed steel module with multiple input ports converging into a single outgoing fiber optic connection, representing a centralized queue gate. Hard clean edges, one directional light throwing a long cast shadow from the left, matte muted palette of graphite, slate grey, and cobalt. Recognisable engineered parts including a rack rail and an inspection gate, generous negative space, no text, no molded, engraved or printed lettering, no plain shapes.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, watermarks, UI, printed words, numbers
rationale: The article is about a structural, systemic software shift—moving from decentralized retries to a centralized rate-limiting gate. A component assembly of a modular proxy bay managing multiple inputs beautifully visualizes this architectural constraint without relying on literal text.
cue: one gate in front of that key
subject: a modular routing proxy bay
core_thesis: An agent fleet fails as a queue under latency load, requiring a centralized gate before the shared key rather than individual agent retries.
core_conflict: Uncoordinated parallel agent requests vs shared capacity limits and queueing exhaustion.
composition: extreme asymmetry with the hero assembly off-centre
alt_text: The Shared Key Bottleneck. A modular proxy routing bay on a concrete floor with multiple inputs converging into one.
caption: The Shared Key Bottleneck: Why parallel agents fail without a centralized queue.
